definition: The Lai–Robbins lower bound gives an asymptotic lower bound on the regret that any uniformly good algorithm must incur in the stochastic multi-armed bandit problem.
details: The original result was proved by Tze Leung Lai and Herbert Robbins in 1985 for parametric exponential families. Later work extended the statement to more general classes of distributions.
story: Imagine a video game where the only feedback is the score ticking up or down — and you learn by playing a million rounds. Instead of being told the rules, it discovers them by living with the consequences. The machine is not handed the answers — it tries things, earns a reward or a miss, and slowly figures out what works. Reward, not instructions, is the teacher. That learn-by-reward loop is Lai–Robbins lower bound.
